prompt: Which inequality is shown on the number line below? (An **open** circle means the value itself is **not** included.)

hint: There are **two** endpoints. Look at each circle (open vs filled) separately.
explanation: The shaded segment runs from $-1$ to $2$, so $x$ is **between** these values.
Left endpoint: circle at $-1$ is **closed** → $-1$ **is** included → $-1 \le x$.
Right endpoint: circle at $2$ is **open** → $2$ is **not** included → $x < 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test values
steps: Try $x = -1$: on the closed circle → **included**. So the inequality must accept $-1$ → rules out $-1 < x$.
Try $x = 2$: on the open circle → **not included**. Rules out $x \le 2$.
Try $x = 0$: in the middle of the shaded segment → included ✓.
Only $-1 \le x < 2$ matches all three checks.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compound-inequality shorthand
steps: A "sandwich" inequality $a \le x < b$ packs two conditions: $a \le x$ AND $x < b$.
Always read the **inner** symbol pointing toward $x$: it tells you the relation at that side.
Closed circle → $\le$ or $\ge$. Open → $<$ or $>$. Direction follows the shaded region.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: For a single endpoint: filled $= \le$ or $\ge$; open $= <$ or $>$. Now apply that rule to **both** ends of this segment.
Walk the segment left to right. Each end: is the circle filled or open?
Left circle is **filled** at $-1$ → $-1 \le x$. Right circle is **open** at $2$ → $x < 2$. Combine: $-1 \le x < 2$.
